reason: Attacked and survived. I opened the named edition itself: the Internet Archive scan behind the verifier URL is genuinely Colvin, Letters of John Keats to His Family and Friends (S. C., May 1891), not the unrelated item its identifier suggests. Letter XXII, headed [Burford Bridge,] November 22, 1817, TO BENJAMIN BAILEY; the running head over the sentence is "1817] TO BAILEY 41", so p. 41 is right. The page reads, verbatim and with the capitals and the comma as proposed: I am certain of nothing but of the holiness of the Heart’s affections, and the truth of Imagination. I then tested the suspicious second "of": it is not an OCR ghost. Helen Gardner (The Noble Moor) and Stanley Kunitz (From Feathers to Iron) both quote "certain of nothing but of the holiness of the Heart’s affections", so the reading has independent scholarly currency, and both drop the comma the proposal keeps, which is exactly why naming Colvin matters. Not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory; pre-1999; publishable. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Keats 1 of 3 (April), not banned, and no second Keats anywhere in the four August proposal files. Tag Correspondence is the form of the work. Source line is 137 characters, leads with the name, no dash, no straight quote; quote ends in a full stop and the only apostrophe is curly. The note is honest about Rollins being unopened.
